title: Climate Change Impacts and Solutions
seo_title: Grade 10 Science (SNC2D): Climate Change Impacts and Solutions Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Evidence and indicators of climate change; its impacts on the environment and on people in Canada and the world; and ways to reduce greenhouse gas emissions (mitigation) and to cope with the changes (adaptation). (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 9 and 10: Science (2008), Science, Grade 10, Academic (SNC2D), Strand D: Climate Change)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science (SNC2D) worksheets on climate change impacts and solutions: temperature and CO₂ data, sea level and ice, impacts in Canada, carbon footprints, mitigation and adaptation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rising CO₂ and temperatures change ecosystems, oceans and communities.
key_sub: Mitigation reduces emissions; adaptation reduces harm.
body_html:
How to think about it

Evidence of climate change includes higher average temperatures, rising CO₂ (now more than 420 ppm), shrinking glaciers and Arctic sea ice, rising sea level and ocean acidification. Ice cores and tree rings show how the climate changed in the past.

In Canada, impacts include longer fire seasons, thawing permafrost, shorter ice-road seasons, heavier rainfall and new pests. Mitigation cuts emissions (clean electricity, transit, efficient buildings, carbon pricing); adaptation prepares for change (flood protection, heat plans, new crop varieties).

Example

CO₂ rose from 340 ppm in 1980 to 420 ppm in 2020. Average rise per year?

80 ppm ÷ 40 years

Answer: 2 ppm per year

Example

Is building a sea wall mitigation or adaptation?

It protects against the effect, not the cause.

Answer: adaptation

Common mistakes

  • Thinking one cold winter disproves climate change.
  • Saying melting sea ice is the main cause of sea-level rise: melting land ice and warming water are.
  • Mixing up mitigation and adaptation.

faq.q: Why does sea level rise as the ocean warms?
faq.a: Water expands when it warms, and melting land ice adds more water.
The fall in ocean pH as sea water absorbs extra CO₂, which makes it harder for shellfish and corals to build shells.
